conclusion: Both one-day native history boundaries are shifted backward by one microsecond. LEAN skips the previous source-file date because only its closed last microsecond remains, then rejects the current file record because its EndTime exceeds the shifted end. Under the standard US-equity configuration this loses every one-day window even with source records present.
causal_steps: The source-date enumerator checks only the remaining first-day interval. NY equity is closed during its final microsecond, so source date Jan8 is not enumerated.
A Jan8 Fundamental source item would have EndTime Jan9 00:00 and belong in the logical window, but that file was skipped.
The enumerated Jan9 file has EndTime Jan10 00:00; the strict native upper filter excludes it.
The result is empty before projection, consistent with the zero-row DataFrame and the later 40 empty windows.
